newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU truck charges talks fail.
newsitem.headline: EU truck charges talks fail.

text.p: European Union transport ministers failed on Tuesday to make any progress towards a revised tax system for trucks using motorways in the 15-country bloc, EU diplomats and officials said.
The Dutch, as EU presidents, failed to broker a deal between countries like Germany and Austria, who want higher charges, and Spain, Greece, Ireland, the Netherlands and Portugal, who do not.
There will now be no deal before ministers' next meeting in October, when Luxembourg will have taken over from the Dutch.

Tuesday's talks were to have ironed out objections to a plan drawn up by the EU presidency to set rules for tax systems in each EU state, including the "Eurovignette" circulation tax used in Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.

In the event, talks bogged down on the opt-outs from maximum charges granted to several countries because of their distance from the EU centre, leaving no realistic chance of a compromise on the charges themselves or on Austria's Brenner Pass tolls.
